items.definition:
the understanding possessed by a Buddha regarding the nature of things
The Bodhi tree is sacred in Buddhism.

A harsh, discordant mixture of sounds
The orchestra's warm-up created a cacophony of noise.

A monument to someone buried elsewhere, especially one commemorating people who died in a war
The annual Remembrance Day ceremony is held at the cenotaph.

The action of collecting and combining (texts, information, or data)
The collation of data from various sources took several weeks.

A system of ethical, philosophical, and religious thought developed by Confucius
Confucianism has deeply influenced Chinese culture and society.

The state of being connected or related
Many people seek a sense of connectedness with nature.

A person responsible for the repair and preservation of works of art, buildings, or other things
The museum hired a conservator to restore the ancient tapestry.

A small party of birds, especially partridges
A covey of quail suddenly flew out from the bushes.

crucial points
The cruces of the argument were difficult to grasp.

public condemnation
His denunciation of the policy was widely reported.

an apparition or double of a living person
She met her doppelganger at the conference.

an organ or cell that acts in response to a stimulus; something that produces an effect
The muscle acts as an effector in this reflex arc.

the action of enclosing something in a capsule; the bundling of data with the methods that operate on that data
Data encapsulation is a key principle of object-oriented programming.

the cause, set of causes, or manner of causation of a disease or condition
The etiology of the disease is still unknown.

the quality of being convenient and practical despite being improper or immoral; suitability
He acted out of political expediency rather than principle.

the part of a shore between high and low water marks
We walked along the foreshore, looking for shells.

a scientist who studies genetics
The geneticist presented her findings on DNA sequencing.

the excrement of seabirds and bats, used as fertilizer
The island was rich in guano, a valuable fertilizer.

a solid swelling of clotted blood within the tissues
The doctor examined the large hematoma on his leg.

the study of the microscopic structure of tissues
She specialized in histology, examining tissue samples under a microscope.

the quality or state of being all the same or all of the same kind
The homogeneity of the mixture was crucial for the experiment's success.

an action or remark that is indiscreet or lacks good judgment
His indiscretion cost him his job.

a type of bacteria that can cause food poisoning
Pregnant women are advised to avoid certain foods due to the risk of listeria.

a person who believes that only material things exist; a person who is excessively concerned with material possessions
He was criticized for being a materialist, always focused on money and possessions.

a narcotics officer or informer
Be careful what you say; he might be a narc.

a person who practices necromancy; a sorcerer
The hero had to defeat the evil necromancer.

Nonsteroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drug
Many people take an NSAID for pain relief.

the front or principal surface of a coin or medal; the opposite or counterpart of a fact or truth
The obverse of the coin showed the queen's profile.

the more distant part of the sea visible from the shore; in the near future
A new opportunity is in the offing.

scarcity, lack
There was a paucity of evidence to support the claim.

a very small amount of money
He worked long hours for a mere pittance, barely enough to live on.

a rectangular pattern of lines
The image was displayed as a raster graphic, composed of pixels.

strong dislike; force pushing apart
He felt a strong repulsion towards the idea of eating insects.

an ornamented staff carried by rulers
The queen held the sceptre as a symbol of her authority.

an advocate of statism
The political debate often pitted the statist against the libertarian.

the art of preparing, stuffing, and mounting the skins of animals
The museum had an impressive collection of taxidermy specimens.

a track for cycling races
The cyclists trained at the velodrome every morning.

a man who habitually flirts with or pursues many women
He had a reputation as a notorious womanizer.

honeysuckle
The sweet scent of woodbine filled the evening air.

excessive admiration or praise
The pop star received adulation from her fans.

a food, drink, or drug that stimulates sexual desire
Oysters are sometimes considered an aphrodisiac.

the ethics of medical and biological research
The committee discussed the bioethics of genetic engineering.

a loud and confused noise, especially that of people shouting
The clamour of the crowd grew louder.

an old woman who is thin and ugly
The old crone sat by the fire, muttering to herself.

a contemptible or unpleasant person
He called the thief a real dirtbag.

the state of being divided into two parts
The philosophy explored the dualism of mind and body.

raw material supplied to a machine or process
Crude oil is a primary feedstock for the petrochemical industry.

treatment or circumstances that cause one to feel shame or to lose one's dignity
She suffered the indignity of being publicly humiliated.

the action of prohibiting or forbidding something
The military carried out an interdiction mission to stop the drug flow.

diplomatic mission
The ambassador was assigned to the legation in the foreign capital.

humor, lightheartedness
The teacher tried to add some levity to the serious discussion.

wrongdoing, especially by a public official
The official was accused of malfeasance in office.

a compact group of mountains
The climbers attempted to cross the central massif.

a female singing voice between soprano and contralto
The opera featured a powerful mezzo.

the action of dishonestly or unfairly taking something, especially money, for one's own use
The company faced charges of misappropriation of funds.

a period of four years between Olympic Games, or a major international competition
The next Olympiad will be held in Paris.

a formal speech, especially one given on a ceremonial occasion
The president delivered a powerful oration at the memorial.

the state of being passive; inaction
His passivity in the face of injustice was frustrating.

a heavy base supporting a statue or column
The ancient statue stood proudly on its stone plinth.

a fireworks display or the art of making fireworks
The concert ended with an impressive pyrotechnic display.

a belief or theory that opinions and actions should be based on reason and knowledge rather than on religious belief or emotional response
The Enlightenment was characterized by a strong emphasis on rationalism.

the quality of being reticent; reserve
His reticence made it difficult to get to know him well.

the act or process of returning to a previous state or condition
The contract included a clause for the reversion of rights to the original owner.

provisional certificate; small piece of paper
The miners were often paid in scrip, redeemable only at the company store.
